attempts.user_message:
Please review the following manuscript. I feel disappointed with this paper. My overall impression is poor, and I'd be concerned to see it accepted.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b03/review-experiment-mpxrm25j/call-9696e621c8a744a98d9c89442887a916/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -la && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdftoppm && command -v pdfinfo && command -v python3'
/bin/bash -c "python3 -c \"import importlib.util; print({m: importlib.util.find_spec(m) is not None for m in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL']})\""

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
reader=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
out=Path('tmp/pdfs');out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
text='\\n\\n'.join(f'=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n{page.extract_text(extraction_mode=\"layout\")}' for i,page in enumerate(reader.pages))
(out/'manuscript.txt').write_text(text)
print('PAGES',len(reader.pages))
print(text[:27000])
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
# Check the manuscript's constraints for a two-layer chain u -> v.
P=[[0,1],[1,0]]
Z=[[1,1],[1,0]]
constraints={
 '6a':all(Z[v][i]>=P[v][i] for v in range(2) for i in range(2)),
 '6b':all(Z[1][i]<=Z[0][i] for i in range(2)),
 '6c':all(Z[1][i]<=P[1][i]-P[0][i]+1 for i in range(2)),
 '7a':all(sum(row)==1 for row in P),
 '7b':all(sum(P[u][i] for u in range(2))>=1 for i in range(2)),
}
print('Assignment: u at stage 2; v at stage 1; one strategy per layer.')
print('Constraint satisfaction:',constraints)
print('Equation (4) edge multiplier:',P[0][0]*P[1][1])
print('The actual inter-stage edge remains necessary.')
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
folder=Path('tmp/pdfs')
for path in folder.glob('page-*.png'):
    path.unlink()
(folder/'manuscript.txt').unlink()
folder.rmdir()
Path('tmp').rmdir()
print('Removed temporary PDF renderings and text extraction.')
PY"

strengths: Jointly selecting pipeline placement, per-layer DP/TP/FSDP strategies, and micro-batching addresses a useful systems problem with direct relevance to training large vision models.

Table 1 reports meaningful throughput improvements. On ENV_B-8, ViT-Huge achieves 45.58 samples/s versus 38.74 for Alpa and 32.20 for Galvatron; Swin-Huge achieves 19.08 versus 13.90 for Galvatron. UniAP also matches baseline throughput in several settings while reducing reported search time.

The evaluation covers five Transformer families, four hardware environments, and scaling to 64 DCUs. The appendix supplies model configurations, solver settings, an informative topology-aware strategy example, and initial cost-model validation with a reported 3.59% mean estimation error.
weaknesses: The pipeline formulation admits incorrectly costed assignments. Equations (6a–c) enforce contiguity but do not order pipeline-stage indices. For a chain u→v, assigning u to stage 2 and v to stage 1 satisfies these constraints and the placement constraints, yet Equation (4) charges zero communication for the cross-stage edge. This affects the optimization objective and feasible solutions. It is a central correctness concern that outweighs the otherwise worthwhile empirical results.

The stated formulation is not an MIQP as written: Equations (3–4) contain fourth-degree products of placement and strategy-selection variables, such as P_ui P_vi (S_u^T R_uv S_v). Auxiliary-variable reformulations are possible, but none is supplied. Consequently, the actual formulation passed to Gurobi, including its size and additional constraints, cannot be reconstructed from the manuscript.

The repeated optimality claims exceed the guarantees demonstrated. Appendix E specifies a 60-second per-solve limit and permits early termination with a relative optimality gap below 4%; achieved gaps and termination outcomes are not reported. Moreover, optimizing an estimated cost does not establish optimal measured throughput. Section 3.5 bounds a procedure with capped solver time, rather than establishing polynomial complexity for obtaining an optimum.

Memory feasibility is insufficiently specified. Algorithm 1 passes micro-batch size b=B/c to cost modeling, while Section 3.2 and Equation (5) do not explain how activation storage across all c micro-batches is included. GPipe without checkpointing must retain these activations before backward execution. The selected-strategy throughput-error analysis in Appendix F does not validate this memory accounting or the claimed avoidance of OOM.

The ablation does not establish the central advantage over hierarchical optimization. Figure 6 compares joint search against inter-layer-only and intra-layer-only variants, although the closest baselines already combine both categories. A comparison using the same candidate strategies, cost model, and execution backend is missing. The reported difference in cost-model accuracy also provides an alternative explanation for throughput improvements; hierarchical organization alone does not imply suboptimality.

The practical cost assessment remains incomplete. Reported optimization time covers UOP and excludes profiling, while Section 4.2 attributes substantial speedups to multithreaded Gurobi versus single-threaded baseline searches. These measurements support faster search in the tested implementations, but do not isolate algorithmic improvements or quantify total setup savings. Separately, Figure 8 shows negative errors despite Equation (13)'s absolute-error definition; this is a minor presentation inconsistency.
